Description: 36 V, 3 A synchronous buck converter, 400 kHz
Notes / why this part: Copy the datasheet layout exactly: C_IN on the same side, tight VIN-PGND loop, small SW node, thermal pad to GND. Digi-Key qty-1 line is the tube LMR33630ADDA (296-48844-ND); ADDAR is the same die on a 2500-pc reel.

Description: Priority power multiplexer, 2.5 A, low R_ON
Notes / why this part: VIN1 = buck (priority), VIN2 = USB. Never sees the motor rail. A FET mux rather than a diode-OR because it wins twice over: no forward drop, so 5V_SYS stays at a full 5.0 V, and the buck wins by construction instead of by whichever source happens to be higher.

Rating verified against datasheet: V_IN 15 V abs, 1 A, dropout 1.3 V
Notes / why this part: 0.85 W worst case from 5 V: needs a copper pour under the tab, not just the footprint. Digi-Key stocks the UMW AMS1117-3.3 (4518-AMS1117-3.3CT-ND), not the original AMS reel.

Description: Wi-Fi + BLE module, 16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM
Notes / why this part: GPIO35/36/37 are consumed by the octal PSRAM. Antenna must overhang the board edge with ≥ 15 mm keepout on all layers.

Rating verified against datasheet: V_VS 4.75-29 V rec (32 V abs), 2.0 A peak
Notes / why this part: Exposed pad MUST be soldered to GND with ≥ 16 thermal vias. Address set by MS1_AD0/MS2_AD1 straps.

Description: N-channel MOSFET, 30 V / 5.7 A, logic level
Rating verified against datasheet: V_DS 30 V, V_GS(th) 1.45 V max, R_DS(on) 31 mΩ at 4.5 V
Notes / why this part: Q1 is the TMC2209 ENN pull-down: its source is ENN_RTN, so it can only pull the shared ENN low when DRV_EN is high AND e-stop pole B closes that return. Q2 and Q3 are the two low-side output switches (5 V on J18, 24 V on J19), each with a 1 k gate series and a 10 k gate pull-down. Note 30 V V_DS on the 24 V channel: keep D3's flyback loop short. AOS AO3400 is obsolete on Digi-Key; order the UMW AO3400A (4518-AO3400ACT-ND) or use stock.

D1 is the only input protection device on the board and does two jobs. Surge clamp: 26 V standoff clears a 24 V rail. Reverse-polarity crowbar: because it is unidirectional, a backwards input forward-biases it and it opens F1 - one fuse instead of one board. Note that the 42.1 V clamp voltage is ABOVE the TMC2209 32 V and LMR33630 38 V limits, so a sustained overvoltage is survived only by blowing F1, not by clamping. Feed this board 12-24 V.

D2/D3 are the OUT1 and OUT2 flybacks, and the only clamp on either channel: the discrete AO3400A switches have no internal clamp. D6 sits in series in the WS2812 5 V feed and drops the strip's VDD by one Schottky drop; that helps 3.3 V data but is not a guaranteed level shift, so fit a 3.3 V-compatible strip or an AHCT buffer. 60 V covers the 24 V rail; using the same part on 5 V means one line item.

D4 only: lights when the buck's PGOOD pin is LOW, i.e. "5 V rail bad". It runs off 5V_BUCK, so it only lights while the buck is up but out of regulation; a dead buck leaves it dark. Firmware state is the addressable pixel on J20.

Description: Dual-line USB ESD protection with V_BUS clamp
Notes / why this part: Place within 5 mm of J4, D+/D- straight through, no stubs.
The three rail indicators only: VMOTOR, 5 V and 3V3. Firmware status is the pixel on J20, not an LED here.

Description: Power inductor, carbonyl powder core, 15.5 mΩ max
Notes / why this part: Sized for 3 A output with headroom at 400 kHz; shielded so it can sit near the ADC island. KiCad has no SRP1265A footprint: Omnimotion:L_Bourns_SRP1265A follows the Bourns recommended layout (two 4.6 × 8.0 mm pads, 5.0 mm gap). Not pad-compatible with the SRP1245A or the Coilcraft XAL6060.

Description: Fast-acting cartridge fuse in a replaceable SMD holder
Rating verified against datasheet: 6.3 A, 125 V AC/DC, 50 A breaking, 9.17 A²s melting I²t
Notes / why this part: 6.3 A is the IEC value: the 154 series steps 5 / 6.3 / 7 A and has no 6 A part at all. Fast-acting because the pre-assembled 154T range stops at 5 A, which puts inrush on the critical path: charging the 1.1 mF of VMOTOR bulk from 24 V costs V²C/2R ≈ 3 A²s at 100 mΩ of source-plus-ESR against a 9.17 A²s melting I²t, but only ~1.4x margin if the supply and leads are very stiff. Cold-start the finished board a dozen times on the real supply before trusting it; if it ever opens on power-up, the holder takes any Nano2, so the 6.3 A Slo-Blo 045406.3MR (75 A²s) is a fuse swap rather than a board change and costs no rating. Replaceable rather than soldered, which matters on a board you will be reworking. Do not go above 6.3 A: the 2.54 mm input terminal is a 6 A part. A resettable PTC was considered and rejected: nothing exists at 24 V with a 6 A hold, and 50 mΩ of post-trip resistance at 6 A is real loss.
Supports the conservative 500 mA USB-only board budget. This thermal PTC is not a precision current limiter; external loads must remain off on USB power.

Rating verified against datasheet: 0.1 A hold, 0.25 A trip, 60 V, 1.5 Ω min
Notes / why this part: Feeds pin 1 of the six endstop connectors only, so a pinched hall-sensor cable trips F3 instead of collapsing 3V3 under the ESP32. Six DRV5033 at 3.6 mA leave 4× margin; move up a size if you fit thirstier sensors. Unused when the endstops are plain switches.

E-stop, EN, BOOT, ENN, UART-idle, PGOOD and mux-ST pull-ups; endstop pull-ups; TMC2209 VREF lower leg and MS1/MS2 address straps; VMOTOR monitor lower leg; VMOTOR LED ballast; Q1 gate-source and the two output-FET gate pull-downs.
Buck FB top, buck EN/UVLO lower leg, TPS2116 PR1 top, the VMOTOR monitor divider into GPIO1, and the three DIAG pull-downs R62-R64, which stay fitted when a driver is left off.
LMR33630 EN/UVLO top. 750 k / 100 k → ~10.5 V start, matching a 12-24 V input.
LMR33630 FB lower. Datasheet 5.0 V table: V_OUT = 1.0 × (1 + 100 k / 24.9 k).
Endstop/analogue RC series, TMC UART TX series, output-FET gate series, PGOOD LED and 5 V rail LED ballast.
TMC2209 VREF top leg and the TPS2116 PR1 lower leg.
USB-C CC1/CC2 pull-downs. One resistor per CC pin, never shared.

Description: Power metal strip current-sense resistor, 1 W
Notes / why this part: TMC2209 BRA/BRB sense. 1 % or better, low inductance; board continuous limit is 1.4 A_RMS/axis.
I²C bus pull-ups (R38/R39) only.
3V3 LED ballast and WS2812 series termination.

Description: Aluminium electrolytic, low ESR, FK series, 10 × 10.2 mm SMD can
Notes / why this part: The only electrolytic: two on VMOTOR and one per TMC2209 VS. SMD can, reflow-friendly.

References: C3 C7 C8 C32 C40 C48
Notes / why this part: VMOTOR and TMC VS ceramic bulk. 50 V part on a 24 V rail loses ~30 % to DC bias - that is budgeted.
Universal decoupling, endstop and analogue-input RC filters and C_BOOT. 50 V rating covers VMOTOR-side use.
LMR33630 high-frequency input bypass. Datasheet-fixed value; place directly across VIN and PGND.
LMR33630 VCC bypass. Use the datasheet value and place directly between VCC and AGND.
LMR33630 output (4 × 22 µF), TPS2116 output and the RGB head-of-strip reservoir.
5 V / 3V3 bulk, ESP32 EN and USB. Nothing smaller than 0805 on this rail.
AMS1117 output. Deliberately tantalum: the LDO loop wants some ESR and can ring on a pure MLCC.
TMC2209 5VOUT bypass, at the top of the datasheet's recommended 2.2-4.7 µF range.
TMC2209 charge pump CPO-CPI. Datasheet-fixed value, do not substitute.

Description: DC power jack, mates standard 5.5 / 2.1 mm plugs
Notes / why this part: Through-hole jack; its normally-closed switch contact (pin 3) is unused. 3.5 A is its rating - use J2 for anything above that, including a full three-motor load.

Description: PCB screw terminal block, tension sleeve
Notes / why this part: J2 DC input, J18 (5 V) and J19 (24 V) outputs. 6 A makes J2 the input ceiling, just under F1's 6.3 A; a three-motor load at 12-24 V draws well under that. 0.5 mm² (20 AWG) is the largest wire it takes.

Description: PCB screw terminal block, tension sleeve
Notes / why this part: J3 2-pole e-stop (A1/A2 to firmware, B1/B2 in the ENN return), J21 auxiliary power take-off.
Mid-mount tabs must be soldered; the shield is the mechanical anchor. Digi-Key cut-tape SKU is the USB4105-GF-A-120 pack (same connector).

Description: Breakaway pin header strip, single row, snapped to length
Notes / why this part: Buy ONE strip - the Qty column counts headers, not strips. Snap it into 3 × 4-way (J5 debug UART, J6 OLED, J7 I²C expansion: 3V3 / GND / SDA / SCL) and 7 × 3-way (J11-J16 endstops 3V3 / GND / SIG, J17 analogue in 3V3 / GND / AIN), using 33 of the 40 pins. Through-hole, so these go on with an iron after reflow like the screw terminals - which also makes them far harder to tear off than an SMT pad when a sensor cable gets yanked.

Description: Pin header, single row, mates a 1×4 Dupont housing
Notes / why this part: Motor phases A+ A- B+ B-. 3 A per pin covers the 1.4 A_RMS (2 A peak) board limit. Unkeyed: mark pin 1 on the housing, and never plug or unplug a motor with the board powered - that kills TMC2209s.

Description: PCB screw terminal block, tension sleeve
Notes / why this part: J20 addressable RGB strip (+5 V / DATA / GND).

Description: SPST-NO tactile switch, 250 gf, gull wing
Notes / why this part: SW1 RESET, SW2 BOOT strap. No runtime user button. Any 2-pin "3 × 6 × 2.5 mm" SMD tactile switch has this outline.
USB shield to GND. Replace with 1 MΩ ∥ 4.7 nF if the shield must float.

References: TP1 TP2 TP3 TP4 TP5 TP6 TP7 TP8 TP9 TP10 TP11 TP12 TP13 TP14 TP15
Notes / why this part: Test points. Bare 1 mm pads with 2 mm keepout; probe rings are optional (Keystone 5015 fits if you want a loop).

Description: 4-layer FR-4, 1.6 mm, 1 oz outer / 1 oz inner, ENIG
Notes / why this part: L1 signal, L2 solid GND, L3 power planes, L4 signal + GND fill. ENIG for the QFN and the module pads.
Plated and tied to GND; the chassis is the EMI return for the motor cables.

Description: Adhesive heatsink with a 6 x 6 mm maximum base
Notes / why this part: Optional above ~1.2 A_RMS per axis. Centre the base on the TMC2209 with electrically insulating thermal adhesive and check clearance to the adjacent capacitors.
